Question:
Why does VGG use small 3x3 convolutional filters?

Answer:
answer: VGG uses very small 3×3 convolution filters in all layers, which makes it feasible to increase network depth by adding more convolutional layers [1]. The paper's main contribution is a thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth using an architecture with very small (3×3) convolution filters, which shows a significant improvement over prior-art configurations by pushing depth to 16–19 weight layers [2]. The 3×3 size is described as the smallest size to capture the notion of left/right, up/down, and center [4]. Using a stack of three 3×3 conv. layers instead of a single 7×7 layer incorporates three non-linear rectification layers instead of a single one, making the decision function more discriminative [10]. It also decreases the number of parameters: a three-layer 3×3 stack with C channels is parametrised by 27C² weights, whereas a single 7×7 conv. layer would require 49C² parameters, i.e. 81% more [6]. This can be seen as imposing a regularisation on the 7×7 conv. filters, forcing them to have a decomposition through the 3×3 filters with non-linearity injected in between [6].

Question:
Why does VGG use small 3x3 convolutional filters?

Answer:

response.answer: VGG uses very small 3×3 convolution filters in all layers, which makes it feasible to increase network depth by adding more convolutional layers [1]. The paper's main contribution is a thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth using an architecture with very small (3×3) convolution filters, which shows a significant improvement over prior-art configurations by pushing depth to 16–19 weight layers [2]. The 3×3 size is described as the smallest size to capture the notion of left/right, up/down, and center [4]. Using a stack of three 3×3 conv. layers instead of a single 7×7 layer incorporates three non-linear rectification layers instead of a single one, making the decision function more discriminative [10]. It also decreases the number of parameters: a three-layer 3×3 stack with C channels is parametrised by 27C² weights, whereas a single 7×7 conv. layer would require 49C² parameters, i.e. 81% more [6]. This can be seen as imposing a regularisation on the 7×7 conv. filters, forcing them to have a decomposition through the 3×3 filters with non-linearity injected in between [6].
